newsitem.title: USA: Central and South West seeks lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Central and South West seeks lower rates.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said its Central Power and Light Company subsidiary is seeking approval from Texas regulatory authorities to lower its retail-base rates.

The unit has filed a request with the Public Utility Commission of Texas to restore most of its retail-base rates to the levels that existed prior to implementation of the rate increase put into effect under bond in May 1996.
The only two exceptions to the request would be industrial interruptible rates and customer service charges.

The commission's March 31 final order approved an increase for these rates at the bonded level or higher. Commissioners on June 20 ordered several modifications to the March 31 final order and decided to re-hear some issues associated with the rate case.

CPL said it anticipates that the commission will issue a new final order incorporating the results of the June 20 modifications, as well as the decisions reached after re-hearing of other issues, by the end of August.
The purpose of CPL's motion is to have the commission amend its June 25 approval of a process that would put into place in mid-July its earlier March 31 final order.

If approved, CPL's motion would lower the level of rates currently being collected by about $65 million, it said. CPL said it anticipates that the final rate level approved by the commission will be put into effect no earlier than November.

Based on its preliminary calculations, CPL said it expects that the commissioners' June 20 decision could result in a final rate reduction on an annual basis of between $3 million to $25 million, as compared with the approximately $27 million reduction ordered in the commission's March 31 final order.

Restoring base rates to their pre-bonded levels as CPL is requesting would decrease the average monthly bill of a residential customer who uses 1,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity per month to about $78.37 from about $83.21, it said.
Implementing the March 31 rate reduction would result in the average monthly bill of that same customer being reduced to about $74.08.
